REEVA'S FAMILY: A NEW BEGINNING

By: Este de Klerk | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Eight months have passed since Reeva's killer was sent to prison. But in only two more, he will be released on correctional supervision. How do Reeva's family pick up the pieces and start over?

Summary:
Eight months have passed since Reeva's killer was sent to prison. But in only two more, he will be released on correctional supervision. How do Reeva's family pick up the pieces and start over?

Only ten months after Oscar Pistorius was sent to jail for the killing of Reeva Steenkamp, he would be released on correctional supervision. It would have been ten months for him behind bars, incarcerated, without the freedom of talking to his loved ones on a daily basis, without the freedom to do what he wishes. But for Reeva's family, it has been 30 months since she has been ripped out of their lives - incarcerated in that reality forever.

Further information:
After having gone through the tormenting court case that lasted eight months and had the eyes of the world focused on them every day, watching their every move, they had to move on. They had to find peace and a way to face the reality they now had to live with.
How does one pick up the pieces after that - a killing, and a very public trial?

June has written a book about it and she has spoken about it, also to us. She says she has forgiven him and doesn't want Oscar to suffer. But is she still suffering every day and how does she feel that he would be released on correctional supervision after only ten months behind bars, despite her and Barry's letter to the parole board?

Kim Martin, Reeva's cousin who was also in court every day and has testified in aggravation of sentence, saying that Oscar has destroyed her family, has not been very public about her feelings since the court case. She has never done a television interview and immediately after the trial said she didn't want to grant any interviews, she and her family just wanted to move on with their lives.

But she is ready to talk now, she is ready to say how she feels about Oscar going to be released on correctional supervision, about Reeva and how her own family are picking up the pieces and moving on.

Press Release:


Reeva’s Family
On the 21st of August this year Oscar Pistorius will be released from prison under correctional supervision, having served ten months in prison for killing his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp in February 2013. With a month to go before his release, Carte Blanche speaks to those closest to the family; Kim Martin (Reeva’s first cousin) and Jennifer Strydom (close friend of June and Barry Steenkamp) for candid insight into the family’s prolonged grief as they contemplate the news of Oscar’s pending house arrest.


Script:


SUGGESTED STUDIO INTRO:

On the 21st of August Oscar Pistorius will be released from prison under correctional supervision – or house arrest. Our Criminal Procedures Act allows for an offender sentenced to imprisonment of five years or less to be considered for correctional supervision after serving one sixth of the sentence – and for Oscar that means ten months. Tonight we hear first-hand from the Steenkamp’s family.

REEVA’S FAMILY: PICKING UP THE PIECES

PRODUCER: ESTé DE KLERK

[START WITH 2SEC OF PICTURE OF REEVA AND MUSIC]

KIM MARTIN: Maybe it’s the way of coping, but you start asking questions, you know. What was the meaning of Reeva’s life, what was her purpose here? You start looking at things like that, but something like this definitely takes a whole family and just turns it completely upside down.

JENNIFER STRYDOM: Reeva has passed on but what one doesn’t understand actually, you might as well say Barry and June – it’s killing them, it’s killing them.

It’s been almost two and a half years since Reeva Steenkamp died…

And after a trial that lasted seven months, her boyfriend Oscar Pistorius was sent to prison in October last year for shooting and killing her.

Reeva’s family members were present in court every day: her mother, June - supported by her best friend, Jennifer Strydom - and Reeva’s cousin, Kim Martin - supported by her husband, Dion.
Her dad, Barry, suffered a stroke just before the trial started and only attended the verdict and sentencing.

JOHN LINK: Now they are facing the prospect of Oscar being released on correctional supervision and that will present another diversion on their journey towards emotional healing.

For those closest to Reeva the passage of time since her violent death, has done little to heal the hurt.

KIM: I don’t think it’s getting easier definitely not, the trial was very, very difficult. Everybody’s lives were put on hold.

Jennifer Strydom has been close to Barry and June for three decades.
She was June’s pillar of strength in Pretoria.
Having kept away from all media until now, she agreed to speak to us in Cape Town.

JOHN: Jennifer, from what you described it does seem that Barry and June are worse off emotionally now than they were back then.

JENNIFER: They are existing. They are not living, they are existing. At the moment June is, she is not well. She must have lost two dress sizes. She doesn’t actually want to live anymore. I have to give her the will to live again, because I said now: “Think about Reeva. She will be very upset if the two of us collapse on the chair and just wilt away. She would like us to build houses for the abused women and children, so let us focus on that now, let’s do something, so that she didn’t die in vain.”

JOHN: We haven’t heard from Barry. He was seen in court, obviously in the closing stages of the trial, but Jennifer, he looks like a broken man?

JENNIFER: He is finished, the only thing that keeps him going is, I think, his racehorses, June and the dogs.

In June, the Department of Correctional Services confirmed that the parole board had approved Oscar Pistorius’s release on August 21st this year placing him under correctional supervision. By then, he will have served ten months of his five-year prison sentence.

KIM MARTIN: I never for one minute ever doubted that he would be sitting longer than 10 months, I didn’t.

JOHN: At the moment that’s not weighing you down?

KIM MARTIN: No, not at all no. I don’t ever want to bump into him. I don’t know if I could handle that. The journey that I have taken since sentencing, if he could have travelled this journey he is going to have to answer and he is going to live with himself.

JOHN: And knowing Oscar do you think that’s what’s happened?

KIM MARTIN: No, I hope so and maybe that’s a part of me that maybe is still angry you know, but no.

In November last year, Carte Blanche interviewed June Steenkamp and we’d hoped to speak to her again, but she’s currently recovering from a medical procedure. She told us last year that she’d forgiven Oscar.

JUNE STEENKAMP: I can forgive, but I still feel angry for the way that he shot her. He must just pay for what he has done.

DEVI: How do you want him to pay for what he has done?

JUNE STEENKAMP: Locked up that’s a way of paying. He can’t go around shooting people.

June told us that whether Oscar was released after ten months or not - it wouldn’t bring back Reeva.

JUNE STEENKAMP: It’s not going to change anything for me. Not going to change a thing.

But Jennifer feels differently.

JENNIFER: Reeva is gone, I mean he should be punished and 10 months for killing a human being, even if it’s not Reeva behind the door and it’s a burglar as he said, I mean, you don’t just get ten months.

Testifying off-camera in aggravation of sentence at the trial, Kim gave Reeva a voice.

KIM: I believe 100% that Reeva picked me up walked me to that stand and was with me the whole time.

She broke down when she recalled how she’d first heard on the radio that Oscar Pistorius had shot his girlfriend.

KIM: I remember saying to my husband: “I hope to God he is cheating on Reeva.” They hadn’t confirmed her name. I got on my phone and I was calling, calling, calling and she she wasn’t answering. I arrived at my mother’s house and she was hysterical and I knew it was true.

She testified that her family wasn’t seeking revenge, but the punishment had to fit the crime.

KIM TESTIFYING: To shoot somebody behind a door, that is unarmed, that is harmless, needs sufficient punishment for

JOHN: So is ten months’ punishment enough?

KIM MARTIN: I think the only person that can answer that is Oscar. He will know whether that has been enough time for him to amended, to make amends in his life.

The Steenkamp family members are now focussed on moving on with their lives. While the trial may have brought a degree of closure it put their grief on hold.

KIM MARTIN: You sit there listening to everything going on in court, but there is so many other emotions. And the day my husband and I left Pretoria for the last day we spent there, I remember thinking to myself: “Now I am grieving,” and it only kicked in then.

JOHN: It always struck me that you seemed in charge, you seemed in control under those circumstances, those situations and you seemed to be marching forward and you almost had a sense that you were trying your best to protect June?

JENNIFER STRYDOM: I had to protect her. Poor June you know I just want to put my arms around her all the time and comfort her because when we would go home at night she would sit and she would say: “Is Reeva really gone?”

June explained how she had to restrain her emotions in court.

JUNE: I didn’t want anybody to see me showing any emotion or picking up on how I felt. I didn’t talk to anyone, I didn’t speak to anyone and I kept my, I tried to keep my dignity,

But away from prying eyes and the cameras and comforted by a dear friend, June could just be herself.

JENNIFER: When we would leave, June would actually cry, she would say: “I cant believe we are here, we are here in Pretoria

Kim Martin, Reeva's cousin who was also in court every day and has testified in aggravation of sentence, saying that Oscar has destroyed her family, has not been very public about her feelings since the court case. She has never done a television interview and immediately after the trial said she didn't want to grant any interviews, she and her family just wanted to move on with their lives. But she is ready to talk now, she is ready to say how she feels about Oscar going to be released on correctional supervision, about Reeva and how her own family are picking up the pieces and moving on.
